description: The Green Infrastructure Framework is Natural England's national guidance and mapping resource for planning good quality green infrastructure in England, and its Green Infrastructure Mapping Database shows where greenspace and habitats are and how well communities can reach them. It covers England, with modules for accessible green infrastructure and the Accessible Greenspace Standard, urban habitat mapping, naturalness factors for accessible parcels in several regions, and access-to-nature scenarios at Output Area level; the framework sets five standards, including the Urban Greening Factor (0.4 for residential development) and the Urban Tree Canopy Cover Standard. It is produced by Natural England, launched on 2 February 2023 with Defra as part of the Natural Capital Ecosystems Assessment programme, and version 2.2 of the mapping database was announced in October 2025. The maps are available free in an online viewer, with generalised data publicly available as a downloadable package; detailed data such as urban habitat classes are available to Public Sector Geospatial Agreement licensees through data sharing. The licence for the public layers is not stated on the pages read. Caveats: some modules cover only parts of England, and individual dataset downloads were still being moved to the Defra Data Sharing Platform. It supports green-blue infrastructure planning, heat and flood adaptation and equitable access analysis; a related record is the London Green Infrastructure Framework.
